title: Optimal bank capital: a trade-off corporate finance perspective
core_idea: Develop a trade-off corporate finance model for banks that quantifies how equity affects the bank's weighted average cost of capital (WACC) by balancing costs (loss in present value of debt tax shields and liquidity premium) against benefits (reduced failure probability); incorporate distress via Fernandez's cost-of-leverage adjusted for liquidity premium and debt policies, and use the Merton model to numerically derive optimal bank capital and capital requirements across firm- and country-specific characteristics.
tldr: A modeling framework that integrates cost-of-leverage and Merton approaches to determine how equity levels influence bank funding costs and to compute optimal capital and capital requirement profiles for different asset, debt, tax and liquidity conditions.
